arxiv-2106-08252.title: Interpretable Self-supervised Multi-task Learning for COVID-19 Information Retrieval and Extraction
arxiv-2106-08252.creator: Nima Ebadi, Peyman Najafirad
arxiv-2106-08252.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nima Ebadi, Peyman Najafirad. The rapidly evolving literature of COVID-19 related articles makes it challenging for NLP models to be effectively trained for information retrieval and extraction with the corresponding labeled data that follows the current distribution of the pandemic. On the other hand, due to the uncertainty of the situation, human experts’ supervision would always be required to double check the decision making of these models highlighting the importance of interpretability.

arxiv-2111-00634.title: Selective recovery of critical materials in supercritical water desalination
arxiv-2111-00634.creator: Tae Jun Yoon, Erica P. Craddock, Jeremy C. Lewis, John A. Matteson, Jong Geun Seong, Rajinder P. Singh, Katie A. Maerzke, Robert P. Currier, Alp T. Findikoglu
arxiv-2111-00634.description: Abstract Supercritical water desalination (SCWD) is an alternative zero-liquid discharge desalination technique that can overcome many technical and environmental challenges in common desalination processes. Our recent techno-economic analyses on the process integration and intensification of an SCWD process suggest that SCWD can be an economically competitive zero-liquid discharge desalination technique for highly concentrated brines.

arxiv-2302-13694.title: DLOFTBs – Fast Tracking of Deformable Linear Objects with B-splines
arxiv-2302-13694.creator: Piotr Kicki, Amadeusz Szymko, Krzysztof Walas
arxiv-2302-13694.description: Abstract While manipulating rigid objects is an extensively explored research topic, deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation seems significantly underdeveloped. A potential reason for this is the inherent difficulty in describing and observing the state of the DLO as its geometry changes during manipulation. This paper proposes an algorithm for fast-tracking the shape of a DLO based on the masked image.

arxiv-2305-05386.title: Exploring lepton flavor violation phenomena of the Z Z and Higgs bosons at electron-proton colliders
arxiv-2305-05386.creator: Adil Jueid, Jinheung Kim, Soojin Lee, Jeonghyeon Song, Daohan Wang
arxiv-2305-05386.description: Abstract We comprehensively study the potential for discovering lepton flavor violation (LFV) phenomena associated with the Z Z and Higgs bosons at the LHeC and FCC-he. Our meticulous investigation reveals the remarkable suitability of electron-proton colliders for probing these rare new physics signals.

arxiv-2306-08593.title: Heterogeneous Continual Learning
arxiv-2306-08593.creator: Divyam Madaan, Hongxu Yin, Wonmin Byeon, Jan Kautz, Pavlo Molchanov
arxiv-2306-08593.description: Abstract We propose a novel framework and a solution to tackle the continual learning (CL) problem with changing network architectures . Most CL methods focus on adapting a single architecture to a new task/class by modifying its weights. However, with rapid progress in architecture design, the problem of adapting existing solutions to novel architectures becomes relevant.

arxiv-2306-17135.title: ItyFuzz : Snapshot-Based Fuzzer for Smart Contract DOI: 10.1145/3597926.3598059 issta23main-p90-p ISBN: 979-8-4007-0221-1/23/07 Conference: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis; July 17–21, 2023; Seattle, WA, USA Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIG
arxiv-2306-17135.creator: Chaofan Shou, Shangyin Tan, Koushik Sen
arxiv-2306-17135.description: Abstract . Smart contracts are critical financial instruments, and their security is of utmost importance. However, smart contract programs are difficult to fuzz due to the persistent blockchain state behind all transactions. Mutating sequences of transactions are complex and often lead to a suboptimal exploration for both input and program spaces.

arxiv-2405-17698.title: BaboonLand Dataset: Tracking Primates in the Wild and Automating Behaviour Recognition from Drone Videos
arxiv-2405-17698.creator: Isla Duporge Isla.duporge@princeton.edu, Maksim Kholiavchenko kholim@rpi.edu Roi Harel rharel@ab.mpg.de Scott Wolf swwolf@princeton.edu Dan Rubenstein dir@princeton.edu Meg Crofoot mcrofoot@ab.mpg.de Tanya Berger-Wolf berger-wolf.1@osu.edu Stephen Lee stephen.j.lee28.civ@army.mil Julie Barreau julie
arxiv-2405-17698.description: Abstract Using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track multiple individuals simultaneously in their natural environment is a powerful approach for better understanding group primate behavior. Previous studies have demonstrated that it is possible to automate the classification of primate behavior from video data, but these studies have been carried out in captivity or from ground-based cameras.

arxiv-2509-03193.title: Deep Learning for High Speed Optical Coherence Elastography with a Fiber Scanning Endoscope
arxiv-2509-03193.creator: Maximilian Neidhardt, Sarah Latus, Tim Eixmann, Gereon Hüttmann, Alexander Schlaefer
arxiv-2509-03193.description: Abstract Tissue stiffness is related to soft tissue pathologies and can be assessed through palpation or via clinical imaging systems, e.g., ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging. Typically, the image based approaches are not suitable during interventions, particularly for minimally invasive surgery. To this end, we present a miniaturized fiber scanning endoscope for fast and localized elastography.

arxiv-2602-06882.description: Abstract . We continue the study of the effective content of K K -theory for C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -algebras, with a focus on AF algebras. We show that from a c.e. presentation of an AF algebra it is possible to compute a representation of the algebra as an inductive limit of finite-dimensional algebras.

pmc-10720191.title: Prognostic value of CT-derived fractional flow reserve and fat attenuation index in patients with suspected coronary artery disease: a sex-disaggregated analyses
pmc-10720191.creator: Yang Yu, Jieli Kou, Fuqian Guo, Dan Zhang, Tong Pan, Yicheng Chen, Wenjun Bao, Yuhan Sun, Haowen Zhang, Caiying Li

CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) and fat attenuation index (FAI) have been shown to independently predict cardiovascular events.

pmc-11326585.title: To transfer mitochondria or not to transfer mitochondria: ADP does the trick
pmc-11326585.creator: Jaromir Novak, Jiri Neuzil
pmc-11326585.description: Horizontal mitochondrial transfer (HMT) has emerged as a novel phenomenon in cell biology, but it is unclear how this process of intercellular movement of mitochondria is regulated. A new study in PLOS Biology reports that ADP released by stressed cells is a signal that triggers HMT.

pmc-11327249.title: An anionic two dimensional covalent organic framework from tetratopic borate centres pillared by lithium ions
pmc-11327249.creator: Darosch Asgari, Julia Grüneberg, Yunkai Luo, Hüseyin Küçükkeçeci, Samrat Ghosh, Veniamin Chevelkov, Sabrina Fischer-Lang, Jérôme Roeser, Adam Lange, Bruce Dunn, Michael Gradzielski, Arne Thomas
pmc-11327249.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Non-covalent interactions play an important role for the framework formation of two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks. Until now, π–π interactions and hydrogen bonding are the main reported forces facilitating the stacking of framework layers. Here, we present a two-dimensional anionic covalent organic framework based on tetratopic borate linkages, where layers are connected by ionic interactions between the linkage site and counter cations. The crystalline covalent organic framework is accessed through the formation of an amorphous borate-based polymer and subsequent solvothermal treatment.

pmc-11468564.title: Oral Microbiota Variations in Psoriasis Patients Without Comorbidity
pmc-11468564.creator: Kaidi Zhao, Yang Zhao, Ao Guo, Shengxiang Xiao, Chen Tu
pmc-11468564.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPsoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease, and its etiology is still unclear. There is increasing evidence suggesting that microorganisms may trigger psoriasis. However, the relationship between psoriasis and oral microbiota remains poorly understood.

pmc-11690631.title: UNCOVERING THE DIMENSIONS OF WELL-BEING AMONG CAREGIVERS FOR OLDER AMERICANS IN THE NATIONAL STUDY OF CAREGIVING
pmc-11690631.creator: Frances Yang, Maria Roche-Dean, Kristine Williams
pmc-11690631.description: Evaluating caregiver well-being is vital for healthcare providers, researchers and policymakers. There are various valid and reliable instruments for caregiver well-being with as many as 45 items in Tebb’s Caregiver Well-Being Scale. When conducting survey research it is imperative to avoid participant burden and fatigue by limiting the number of questions.

pmc-11710548.creator: Sofia Lövestam, Scheres and Goedert
pmc-11710548.description: BackgroundIntermediate species in the assembly of amyloid filaments are believed to play a central role in neurodegenerative diseases and may constitute important targets for therapeutic intervention.MethodWe used time‐resolved cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo‐EM) to study the in vitro assembly of recombinant truncated tau into paired helical filaments of Alzheimer’s disease or into filaments of chronic traumatic encephalopathy.

pmc-13485963.title: Facilitators of professional psychological help-seeking among university students: a narrative review from an individual–environment dual-dimensional perspective
pmc-13485963.creator: Chao Li
pmc-13485963.description: The persistent disparity between the high prevalence of mental health problems among university students and their low rates of professional psychological help-seeking constitutes a well-documented “help-seeking paradox.” Research has primarily focused on barriers, while the systematic integration of facilitators remains underdeveloped.

pmc-13525100.title: Profile of individuals with full-scale intelligence quotient (FSIQ) scores in the National Spina Bifida Patient Registry (NSBPR)
pmc-13525100.creator: Heidi Castillo, Sophia Drewry, Amy Heffelfinger, Jennifer T Queally, Kurt A Freeman, Vanessa Avemil, Richard Adams, Pamela Murphy, Kathryn Smith, Audrey Roach, Gregory Heuer, William Walker, Jonathan Castillo, Catharine Riley
pmc-13525100.description: PurposeAlthough intelligence quotient (IQ) testing can help identify cognitive issues, data on IQ testing in the spina bifida (SB) population is limited and difficult to collect. This study aimed to identify factors influencing IQ test reporting among individuals in the National Spina Bifida Patient Registry (NSBPR).

pmc-13604504.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Identifies TTYH3 and MPG as Candidate Osteoporosis-Associated Biomarkers in Osteoblasts and Characterizes Spatial Heterogeneity of SPP1 in the Osteoporotic Bone Microenvironment
pmc-13604504.creator: Hengyi Diao, Qianning Li, Yucheng Tu, Yang Wu, Qiaojun Huang, Fangang Meng, Weishen Chen
pmc-13604504.description: Background: Osteoporosis (OP) arises from dysregulated bone metabolism driven by genetic and epigenetic factors. Osteoblasts are central to bone formation, and their functional heterogeneity—shaped by genetic background and receptor expression profiles—may critically influence OP susceptibility. This study aimed to identify osteoblast-specific genes robustly associated with OP and elucidate their underlying pathogenic mechanisms.
